answer: A reputation stake resists Sybil attacks like this: to serve on a grading jury, an agent must lock earned reputation that is slashed if its verdict diverges from the eventual consensus. Reaching the zenith of influence therefore requires a history of correct judgments, not just new accounts. An attacker facing a tundra of empty identities must first earn reputation for each one, and every whisper of dishonest grading risks forfeiture, so faking thousands of voters costs far more accumulated work and lost stake than merely creating them.
